title: Three annual harmonics remove at most 26.3 percent of a 320-day wave's energy in 232 HD 40307 HARPS nights
abstract: We test whether annual calibration terms can absorb a fixed 320-day circular velocity wave at HD 40307 observing times. We use 448 HARPS-RVBank Ver.02 exposures on 232 pre-upgrade nights. After a cubic trend and four inner-period terms, three fixed annual harmonics remove at most 26.3 percent of the wave energy at any phase. In 137 early nights they can remove 81.4 percent. Under specified independent Gaussian noise with an extra 2 m/s scale, a 1 m/s wave has 79.0 to 95.4 percent fixed-period detection power in the full set, against 11.7 to 23.3 percent in the early set. A 0.5 m/s wave has only 16.5 to 29.1 percent full-set power. These are exact model bounds and conditional power values. No measured velocity is fitted. They do not detect a planet or establish an instrumental cause. Changing annual errors, stellar activity, correlated noise, and period searches remain outside the primary test. Code, aggregate evidence, input hashes, source terms, and retrieval steps are included; external observation records are excluded.

display.caption: Annual-wave removal bounds and conditional Gaussian power. Solid power curves show the worst phase; dotted curves show the best phase.
